html:
The Modoc are a Native American people of the high country on the border of what is now California and Oregon, around Tule Lake and Lower Klamath Lake. They speak a dialect of the Klamath and Modoc language, shared with their neighbours the Klamath.

They lived by fishing the lakes and rivers, hunting waterbirds and deer, and gathering water lily seeds and roots, and they spent winters in earth covered lodges.

In 1864 the Modoc signed a treaty that put them on the Klamath Reservation in Oregon, among their old rivals. Conditions were poor, and a band under Kintpuash, known to settlers as Captain Jack, went back to their homeland on the Lost River. When the army came to move them in 1872, the Modoc War began. A few dozen fighters held out for months in the lava beds south of Tule Lake against a far larger force. During peace talks in 1873 Kintpuash killed General Edward Canby, the only US general killed in the Indian wars. The band surrendered; Kintpuash and three others were hanged, and the rest were exiled to Indian Territory. Some returned to Oregon in 1909.
